description: HLS live streaming origin — FFmpeg transcodes an RTMP ingest or file into a segmented .m3u8 playlist; Nginx serves segments with CORS so browser HLS.js or native Safari players can pull directly. Node control plane lists active streams.

gotchas: Segment duration is a latency/stability tradeoff — 2s segments give ~6s glass-to-glass latency with 3-segment buffer; shorter segments drop glass-to-glass at the cost of more frequent playlist churn and higher client buffering risk on flaky networks.
Browsers require CORS on both the playlist AND every segment. The nginx.conf here adds Access-Control-Allow-Origin to .m3u8 and .ts — stripping either will break HLS.js.
Safari plays HLS natively; Chrome/Firefox need hls.js. Your frontend must feature-detect: `video.canPlayType('application/vnd.apple.mpegurl')` — non-empty means native, else bundle hls.js.
ffmpeg's `-hls_flags delete_segments` is mandatory for a rolling window — without it the origin fills disk with every 2s segment ever transcoded.
RTMP ingest is TCP port 1935, plaintext. Put nginx-rtmp or srtrelay in front if you need auth/TLS; this origin assumes the ingest side is already trusted.

FFmpeg needs hardware-accelerated codec config (h264_videotoolbox on macOS, h264_nvenc on nvidia) for production-scale transcoding. The default libx264 in start-stream.sh is CPU-bound and single-stream only.
